successors.name: Song (state)
successors.text: Teng, 'annihilated by King Kang of Song in 297 BC'; its territory 'corresponds to present-day Tengzhou'

ledger.x: 1046: the Zhou enfeoff Shu Xiu of Cuo, a brother of King Wu, as viscount of Teng in southern Shandong.
333: Yue's hold on Teng ends at the latest with the fall of Yue: 'Yue was partitioned by Chu and Qi in 333 BC' (Yue page; infobox 'Conquered by Chu: 333 BC').
297: King Kang of Song annihilates Teng.

wars.name: Yue conquest of Teng
wars.outcome: Teng conquered by King Zhugou of Yue (414 on the infobox); the page's lead takes 414 as the end of Teng, its text and the Spring and Autumn table keep Teng until 297.

wars.name: Song annihilation of Teng
wars.outcome: Teng annihilated by King Kang of Song; its land goes to Song.

certainty.note: A small viscounty known by its capital Tengzhou; the frontier with Lu, Zhu, Xue and Song is unsurveyed.
